organizer: Rotary International; each club is sponsored by a local Rotary club
organizer_domain_provenance: rotary.org is Rotary International's own first-party global domain, serving the Interact programme pages and the chartering contact address interact@rotary.org. Rotary operates a formal district structure with its own domains — in Türkiye, districts 2420 (İstanbul and Marmara), 2430 (Central/Eastern Anatolia) and 2440 (Aegean), federated at rotary.org.tr — which corroborates the organisational chain from the national end. NOT YET DONE: I did not fetch a Turkish district page confirming a specific Interact club roster. rotary.org is a .org and will fail looksOfficial().
prerequisites: A sponsoring Rotary club is required — 'Rotary club sponsors mentor and guide Interactors as they carry out projects and develop leadership skills'
A Rotary Adviser from the sponsoring club attends regular and board meetings
duration: Ongoing membership; clubs run on an annual cycle
selection_process: Join an existing club — 'Check with your school or contact a local Rotary club to find out if there's an Interact club in your area.' To charter a new club: hold elections for president, vice president, secretary, treasurer and the rest of the board; agree annual club dues; complete the Interact Club Certification Form; list charter members who have agreed to attend at least 60% of the club's service and social activities; obtain the sponsor Rotary club president's and the district governor's signatures; submit to interact@rotary.org. Chartering typically takes two to four weeks.
required_materials: Interact Club Certification Form (for chartering a new club)
award_or_output: A chartered club within a network of 14,911 clubs and 342,953 members across 145 countries; at least two completed service projects per year; a Certificate of Organization issued by Rotary International to the sponsoring club
leadership_evidence: STRONG, AND THE MANDATE IS THE POINT. Rotary's own page states clubs 'organize at least two projects every year, one that helps their school or community and one that promotes international understanding.' That is an externally-imposed delivery obligation, not an aspiration — an Interact club that does nothing is not meeting its charter. Combined with the chartering requirements (elections for president, vice president, secretary and treasurer; a 60% attendance commitment from charter members; district governor countersignature), a student can demonstrate: elected officer of a club chartered by an international organisation, with a documented annual record of at least two completed service projects. The elected office is peer-conferred and the projects are countable — precisely the combination ORYN's leadership scoring is supposed to reward over a self-declared title. ACCESSIBILITY NOTE FOR ORYN: at 145 countries this is one of the very few genuinely global leadership-and-service structures, and Rotary's three Turkish districts make it reachable in ORYN's home market — unlike most US-centric leadership programmes in this space.

award_or_output: Membership or office in a chartered club within a network of 7,700+ clubs and 200,000+ Leos across 150+ countries and territories, collectively running 60,000+ service projects each year; a Certificate of Organization for new clubs; eligibility for Leo awards and grants
leadership_evidence: STRONG, WITH AN UNUSUAL CEILING. Lions International states directly that 'Leos have many leadership opportunities, including the ability to serve as Leo officers in their club, district and multiple district through annual elections.' The escalation past club level is what distinguishes this from an ordinary school club: a 16-year-old can hold elected district office across many clubs, which is a genuinely uncommon scope of responsibility at that age. Chartering itself requires a formation meeting at which members adopt a constitution and elect officers, followed by a formal installation ceremony — the office is constitutionally defined, not informal. There is also a named advisory route: the Leo Club Program Advisory Panel seats two Leos per constitutional area in monthly meetings with Lions International staff to shape the programme. A student can demonstrate: elected club, district or multiple-district officer; N service projects delivered; and, at the top of the ladder, a seat advising an international organisation's staff. ACCESSIBILITY NOTE FOR ORYN: 150+ countries and territories, and the sponsorship model means a student's route in is finding a local Lions club — which exists in most Turkish and European cities.

canonical_name: İstanbul Kent Konseyi Gençlik Meclisi — Gençlik Katılım Ağı
organizer: İstanbul Kent Konseyi (Istanbul City Council) — Gençlik Meclisi
organizer_domain_provenance: DIRECT AND OBSERVED. The footer of istanbulkentkonseyi.org.tr reads 'İstanbul Kent Konseyi - İBB Bilgi İşlem Dairesi Başkanlığı tarafından tasarlanmıştır' — the site is stated on its own pages to have been built by İstanbul Büyükşehir Belediyesi's Information Technology Department, tying the .org.tr domain directly to the metropolitan municipality. The membership form's district dropdown enumerates exactly İstanbul's 39 districts, consistent with a municipal body. Kent konseyleri are themselves statutory bodies established under Turkish municipal law rather than voluntary associations. NOTE: the site presented an untrusted TLS certificate to a server-side fetcher and had to be read through a browser. It is a .org.tr and will fail looksOfficial().

age_range.quote: İstanbul'da yaşayan 16-29 yaş aralığında gençlerin içerisinde yer aldığı
age_range.note: Residency in İstanbul is part of the stated criterion. Only 16-18 of ORYN's 14-18 band qualifies.

grade_range: The live application form's Öğrenim Durumu dropdown includes 'Lise' (high school) alongside İlköğretim, Orta Öğretim and higher levels, so secondary students are explicitly catered for
selection_process: Open registration via the Gençlik Meclisi application form on the site (name, birth date, field/occupation, school/university, education level, existing civil-society volunteering or memberships, contact details, İstanbul district, acceptance of participation conditions and the KVKK privacy notice). No competitive selection is described.
award_or_output: Membership of the Gençlik Katılım Ağı; the site invites young people to take part in its events and projects 'katılımcı olarak ya da görev alarak' (as a participant or by taking on a role)
latest_verified_cycle: Form live and accepting applications on 2026-08-21; the birth-year dropdown begins at 2010, consistent with the stated 16-year minimum
leadership_evidence: MODERATE — AND I AM DELIBERATELY NOT OVERSTATING IT. What the official page evidences: this is a statutory municipal youth body, founded June 2021, whose stated purpose is to identify young people's problems, needs and proposed solutions about city life and 'yerel yönetimde bu tespitlere yönelik gençlik politikalarının üretilmesine katkı sunmak' — to contribute to the production of youth policy in local government. Membership therefore puts a 16-year-old inside a real municipal policy channel, which is a genuinely different thing from a school club. What the page does NOT evidence, and what I therefore will not claim: any election, any executive board (yürütme kurulu) seat, or any defined office. The page describes open registration to a participation network and an invitation to take on roles at events, nothing more. A student can honestly claim membership of İstanbul's municipal youth assembly network and whatever specific role they actually took; they cannot claim an elected position on this evidence. A counselor should treat this as a high-quality civic entry point in ORYN's home city, and should ask the student what role they actually held rather than accepting the membership as leadership.

If the statutory basis is confirmed, this is a repeatable record TEMPLATE across dozens of Turkish cities rather than a single opportunity — a far larger prize than one İstanbul entry, and the reason the mevzuat follow-up matters.

aliases: The International Award for Young People-Türkiye
organizer: TİKAV (Türkiye İnsan Kaynakları Eğitim ve Sağlık Vakfı / Turkey Human Resources Education and Health Foundation), as sole National Award Operator under The Duke of Edinburgh's International Award Foundation
organizer_domain_provenance: intaward.org.tr is the Türkiye operator's own site and self-identifies TİKAV as sole National Authority since 1 June 2013. The parent Foundation's global site is intaward.org. NOT YET DONE, AND THIS IS THE WEAK LINK: I fetched intaward.org/turkey hoping the Foundation itself would name and link the Türkiye operator, and the page returned no operator details — so the chain from the international Foundation down to intaward.org.tr is asserted only from the Turkish end. An ingestion pipeline should confirm via the Foundation's 'The Award near me' country directory before treating intaward.org.tr as official. Both domains are .org / .org.tr and will fail looksOfficial().
eligible_countries: Türkiye (this record); the Award itself operates in more than 130 countries and territories

age_range.quote: all 14 to 24-year-olds, inclusive of all backgrounds, locations, cultures and abilities

prerequisites: Participation is normally through a licensed Award Centre (in Türkiye, schools and institutions operating under TİKAV's national licence)

duration.Bronze: At least 6 months minimum participation required
duration.Silver: At least 12 months minimum participation required (or 6 months if a Bronze Award holder)
duration.Gold: At least 18 months minimum participation required (or 12 months if a Silver Award holder)

selection_process: Not competitive. Enrolment through a licensed Award Centre; the Award is earned by completing the required sections for the level, not awarded by selection.
individual_or_team: individual, with a team component in the Adventurous Journey
award_or_output: Bronze, Silver or Gold Award. Four sections: Voluntary Service ('give service (volunteer) over a set period of time'), Skills, Physical Recreation, and Adventurous Journey (Bronze: two days/one night, minimum 12 hours purposeful effort; Silver: three days/two nights, 21 hours; Gold: four days/three nights, 32 hours). Gold additionally requires a Residential Project of 'at least four nights and five consecutive days' with an unfamiliar group.
latest_verified_cycle: Operating; TİKAV sole National Authority since 1 June 2013
leadership_evidence: GENUINE COMMUNITY-IMPACT EVIDENCE WITH A DURATION FLOOR — which is exactly what makes it useful rather than decorative. Voluntary Service is a mandatory section at every level, and the Award imposes minimum participation periods that cannot be short-circuited: 6 months for Bronze, 12 for Silver, 18 for Gold (or 12 with a Silver already held). A Gold Award holder has therefore, by definition, sustained voluntary service and skill development over at least a year and a half, plus a four-day team expedition and a five-day residential with strangers. HONEST LIMIT: the Award certifies sustained personal commitment and service, not leadership of others. There is no elected role, no team to manage and no project ownership in the framework itself. A counselor should read Gold as strong, verifiable, multi-year community_impact and execution evidence — and should not inflate it into a leadership claim. WHY THIS RECORD MATTERS TO ORYN SPECIFICALLY: the catalogue already holds the Australian Award operator and the Hong Kong Award for Young People, but nothing for ORYN's home market. This is the Türkiye route to the same globally-recognised credential.

LICENCE WORDING — CONFLICT FLAGGED: search results state that in 2013 TİKAV signed a 'License Agreement ... with the International Award Foundation in England'. The intaward.org.tr page I actually fetched says instead that 'TIKAV is a member of The International Award Association recognised by the European Union' and does not use the word licence. These are different claims about the legal relationship and I have not merged them; I have recorded the operator role, which both support, and flagged the licence question as unresolved. DELIBERATE NULLS: cost (neither the Foundation nor the Türkiye operator publishes a participant fee on the pages I read — Award Centres typically set their own, but I found no evidence and will not guess); deadline and programme dates (there are none; enrolment is through a centre and the clock starts when the participant starts); application_url (no direct enrolment route is published — a student must go through a licensed Award Centre); international_applicants_allowed (unstated). NOT A DUPLICATE: ORYN's catalogue holds 'The Duke of Edinburgh's International Award - Australia' and 'The Hong Kong Award for Young People (AYP)'. Those are sibling national operators of the same global Award, not this one. An ingestion pipeline should model these as national operators of one canonical Award rather than as three unrelated opportunities.
